# XY Forever serial protocol 1.22: examples and conformance

Part of the [XY Forever serial protocol 1.22](../PROTOCOL.md).

## Examples

Whole frames in hex, as the device and the host tool encode them (checked by `tests/test_protocol_spec.py`). The spec file also holds byte streams (`streams`)
with the frames a correct parser finds in each: noise before a frame; a bad CRC, then a good frame; a frame split at every byte; two frames back to back; an
oversized length; a frame cut short, then a frame; frames split across reads; an event and a reply back to back; noise and a reply split across reads.

- Hello (`hello` request, seq 1): `58 46 01 01 00 00 00 00 4c 8d 06 32`

## Conformance suite

`protocol/v1.conformance.json` holds the conformance suite: the behaviour a v1 device must show, as data that any client can run. Each case is a named exchange:
preconditions (`given`: a fresh boot before `hello`, files in the test area, simulator faults), requests by command name and field values (or raw bytes for
malformed input and frame-level tests), and what must come back (status, field values, limits such as the device's `read=`), including reads that show what did
not change. Every case says what it does (`effects`: none means read-only; `staging`, `writes_test_area`, `restarts`, `writes_device`, `boots_os`), what it
needs (`needs`: simulator control, fixtures) and whether it is safe on a real device (`real_device`, else `why_not`). The keywords are documented in the file's
`syntax` object.

A third-party client conforms when it runs every case with its own codec and transport: send the requests in order, one at a time, and check each expectation.
Two runners exist: `python3 scripts/conformance.py --sim 127.0.0.1:7341` (or without `--sim` for the OP-XY, where only cases marked safe run and a guard refuses
any request that could change more than the test area `/yaffs2/xy-forever/log/conformance/`), and `node clients/ts/test/conformance.ts --sim 127.0.0.1:7341` for
the TypeScript module. Both read the same file; `--check` only interprets every case.

88 cases: 66 safe on a real device; 41 read-only, 37 use the staging, 22 write the test area, 6 restart the device, 5 change stored state outside it and 3 boot
the OS (simulator only).
